audit.whatIsWrong: All seven phases[N].side read "Skill" while win[0..6] gives Galio five stages then Ekko two, and phases[5]/[6].why still described Galio winning.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Galio x5 then Ekko x2 and matches win[]. Chronobreak drops from 110s to 80s at rank 2 and 50s at rank 3, which is the flip.
audit.corrected: Sides aligned to win[]; the two Ekko rows' whys rewritten with Chronobreak's real cooldowns and ratings dropped to 4/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four content fields attributed Ekko's stun to Timewinder (Q) or Phase Dive (E).
audit.why: The stun is Parallel Convergence (W): the anomaly arms after a few seconds and stuns only if Ekko enters it. Timewinder slows; Phase Dive is a 325-range roll with an attack teleport and no CC.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text, spikes[3].text, early and late all re-attributed to Parallel Convergence.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and neither Chronobreak's untargetability nor its healing reached the page as something to play around.
audit.why: Chronobreak makes him untargetable and heals a percentage of damage received in the rewind window, so damage dumped into it is refunded; Grievous Wounds timing decides the trade. Phase Dive is an auto-reset, so the wind-up — not the cast — is the tell.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns now carries Chronobreak 110s/50s, Parallel Convergence 22s with its walk-in condition, and Phase Dive 9s/325 range; breakdown.late now names Grievous Wounds.

edits.before: - Ekko Chronobreak: matchup-defining — Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Shield of Durand for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Chronobreak: 110s at rank 1, 50s at rank 3 — he goes untargetable, so hold your last damage until he lands. - Parallel Convergence: 22s at rank 1, and the stun only fires if he walks into his own anomaly. - Phase Dive is 9s and only 325 range.

edits.before: Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Phase Dive is 325 range and teleports him onto you on the next attack — start the W charge on the roll, not on the arrival.

edits.before: Q the contact, let the tornado tick, E-auto if he answers, W-taunt the commit — a full rotation where his half landed on a shield.
edits.after: Chronobreak rewinds him to where he stood seconds ago — drop Winds of War on that spot and the tornado is waiting when he lands.

edits.before: That is Ekko’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: His anomaly takes seconds to arm, and a feinted W charge walks you into it.

edits.before: Charging W through a minion line at a mage holding his answer — the statue mid-charge is the lane's easiest skillshot target.
edits.after: Justice Punch is 11s and it is your only answer to Phase Dive — roaming without it means his next dive costs you the wave.

edits.before: Ekko wins by landing Chronobreak, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Ekko wins by stunning you in Parallel Convergence, bursting from Phase Dive range, and rewinding the kill with Chronobreak.

edits.before: Carry through arrivals — Hero's Entrance turns every losing skirmish your team starts into a 5v4 with a knockup.
edits.after: Carry by making his rewind pointless: taunt him inside his own anomaly and Chronobreak brings him back to the same fight.

edits.before: You are the anti-dive: taunt their engage off your carry, shield the magic, and R the flank their comp built around.
edits.after: You are the anti-dive: taunt Ekko off your carry, and carry Grievous Wounds because Chronobreak heals off the damage you just did.

edits.before: First item spike: the full taunt rotation chunks and your MR makes AP trades a subscription you sell.
edits.after: First item: Chronobreak is 80s at rank 2 and heals him out of the burst you just spent everything on.

edits.before: Late Galio is the anti-engage: taunt their dive, shield their magic, and R the teammate they thought was alone.
edits.after: Two items in he flanks with Phase Dive, stuns in his anomaly, and rewinds home on a 50-second Chronobreak.

edits.before: Once Ekko has enough AP to one-shot with Phase Dive into Timewinder stun, his roam-and-burst playstyle starts outscaling your straightforward lane trades.
edits.after: Once Ekko has enough AP to one-shot off a Parallel Convergence stun into Phase Dive, his roam-and-burst playstyle starts outscaling your straightforward lane trades.

edits.before: Ekko can flank your ultimate engage with his own Phase Dive stun and blow up a priority target before your team can follow up, effectively counter-engaging your R.
edits.after: Ekko can flank your ultimate engage by arming Parallel Convergence for the stun and blow up a priority target before your team can follow up, effectively counter-engaging your R.

edits.before: At levels 1-5 Ekko's combo requires a landed Timewinder stun that's slow and easy to sidestep, so your melee trades and Q poke consistently punish his cooldowns and mistakes.
edits.after: At levels 1-5 Ekko's combo needs Timewinder's slow and a Parallel Convergence he must walk into himself, so your melee trades and Q poke consistently punish his cooldowns and mistakes.

edits.before: Late game Ekko becomes a real threat to your engage-first playstyle — his own Phase Dive stun can flank and burst a priority target the instant you commit your ultimate, so you want numbers advantage or vision before diving in.
edits.after: Late game Ekko becomes a real threat to your engage-first playstyle — his Parallel Convergence stun and Phase Dive can flank and burst a priority target the instant you commit your ultimate, so you want numbers advantage or vision before diving in.

notes: Fabricated interactions killed: four content fields gave the stun to Timewinder (Q) or Phase Dive (E). Ekko's only stun is Parallel Convergence (W), and it requires him to enter his own anomaly — that is the actual counterplay and it now reaches the page. Chart sides were all 'Skill' against a correct win[] of Galio x5 / Ekko x2, so only side edits were needed. Anti-heal: report[8].t (Itemization) still does not mention Grievous Wounds against Chronobreak's healing; the report-rewrite cap and the lint (which did not flag it) kept me out of it, so I put it in breakdown.late instead — worth adding to Itemization in a later pass.
